# Review of SEEN-109, attempt 4, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned on opus with the task text of triage record 45 and nothing else. It read
the ticket, all forty-five records, the nineteen files of the focus set, the
review template, three lines of the calibration report and `CLAUDE.md`. It
verified the suspected defects by running the module against its own fixtures
rather than by reading it. `reviewer_session` is null for the reason note 17
gives.

Verdict: **return**, on F1, F2 and F3.

It confirmed the eight findings of the third review as answered, and checked
record 38's failures line for line against what record 44 claims: seven, against
the one plus six the record states.

## The findings

**F1, high, `harness/calibration.py:159`.** The same class of defect as note 17
and note 25, reached through the shape of the reference rather than through
`lstrip`. An unattributable row is written only when `path_of` returns nothing,
so a finding whose file string is anything but an exact member of
`would_exclude` is counted clean. Measured on the module's own fixtures with
`would_exclude` holding `harness/skipped.py`: `harness/skipped.py:12` gives one
escape, `harness/skipped.py:12-20` gives none and nothing unattributable,
`harness/skipped.py:58:5` gives none and nothing, and `harness/typo.py:3` gives
none and nothing. A line range is what a reviewer writes for a hunk, and the
last case is a path the triage never saw at all. The triage record carries
`files` as well as `would_exclude`, so a reference naming neither is detectable
and was not detected.

**F2, medium, `harness/calibration.py:587`.** Evidence nobody can place holds
the report's verdict at stay-shadow and does not return a live triage to shadow,
while the workflow, both skill copies and the report's closing paragraph all say
the triage reads the verdict. Run on a planted tree, the calibration report says
stay-shadow and the weekly report says `In shadow: no` about the same tree, and
reviewers keep reading a narrowed focus set.

**F3, medium, `harness/cli.py:769`.** `--no-findings` discharges the new
requirement in one word and makes the round read clean, and nothing cross-checks
it. Before this attempt a forgotten flag wrote an unattributable row, which now
holds the verdict; after it the cheapest path reads as evidence of no escape.
The reviewer cites this ticket's own journal as the evidence that sessions take
the cheap path: records 18 and 26 carry no findings at all and record 37 carries
an empty list, while notes 17, 25 and 36 record one high and three mediums, one
high and four, and two mediums and six lows. `--findings` existed at commit
150b269, before record 37 was written.

**F4, low, `harness/calibration.py:435`.** No test pins the printed go-live
instruction to naming both lines, so the one-line instruction the third review
returned the ticket on can come back with the suite green.

## The deterministic checks it was handed

`red_before_green` verified line for line rather than by exit code, for every
attempt. `tests_added` passes but for F4. `acceptance_entries` passes.
`slice_files` it passed, noting that `harness/doctor.py` is described in the
Outcome in substance but is not named there among the deviations. `pull_request`
stayed unavailable. It checked the generated copies against their sources and
the ground rules over the whole diff.

## What the shadow window will read from this round

The triage would have excluded 13 of 19 files, 55.76 per cent. F1 lands in
`harness/calibration.py` and F3 in `harness/cli.py`, both files the triage kept,
so neither is an escape; F2 and F4 are at severities that can never be one. The
round reads clean, and the ticket is excluded from the window by name.
